title: Relative perfection of algebraic upper shriek for flat Noetherian algebras
statement: Let $R\to A$ be a flat finite type homomorphism of commutative Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], [def-weil-flat-morphism]. For any polynomial presentation $P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\twoheadrightarrow A$, set $K=R\operatorname{Hom}_P(A,P)[n]\in D(A)$, with the $A$-module structure of derived coinduction [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Then $K$ is pseudo-coherent over $A$, meaning that it is represented by a bounded-above complex of finite free $A$-modules [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex]; it has bounded finitely generated cohomology; and it has finite Tor amplitude over $R$, meaning that there are integers $a\le b$ such that $H^i(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}M)=0$ for all $R$-modules $M$ and all $i\notin[a,b]$. Moreover, the scalar map $A\to R\operatorname{Hom}_A(K,K)$ is an isomorphism. No local complete-intersection hypothesis on $A$ is imposed.
